communityPost.body:
I have a more philosophical question that has been on my mind for some time, but the link to Weekly 81 with the question "would you buy at todays price" reminded me of.

As investors we are typically aiming for investments for the longer (1-year+) term. Such that individual turbulent quarters don't change our approach as long as the thesis is still intact.

There have been many times I would not buy an investment that I already hold at the current price (sometimes it corrected lower, sometimes it didn't). But I also do not try to time the market by selling and rebuying it even if I think it is currently overpriced. It may also be that it is still underpriced but not by enough that it would represent a good risk-reward.

Since equities are liquid, even for a stock that we plan to 'hold' it is equivalent to choosing to buy that stock every single day. How do you resolve that different perspective in light of the 'would you buy today?' question?

Do you have any plans to revisit RYAM and update the model? I've skimmed the last thesis and some of the recent results an earnings, and curious whether you think they're on track with your original thesis or it needs a reset on price targets
